requirements.requirement: Create the appworker account on node1
requirements.summary: useradd -m -s /bin/bash appworker succeeded and id appworker confirms uid=1000(appworker). Account persisted after reboot as confirmed by post-restart id appworker output.

requirements.requirement: Give appworker login sessions a limit of 8,192 open files (nofile)
requirements.summary: /etc/security/limits.d/appworker.conf sets both soft and hard nofile to 8192. PAM pam_limits.so is required in system-auth and password-auth session stacks. Live verification via sudo -u appworker bash -c 'ulimit -n' returned 8192 both before and after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Give appworker login sessions a limit of 256 processes (nproc)
requirements.summary: /etc/security/limits.d/appworker.conf sets both soft and hard nproc to 256. PAM pam_limits.so is required in session stacks. Live verification via sudo -u appworker bash -c 'ulimit -u' returned 256 both before and after reboot.

overall_summary: All three material outcomes are satisfied with strong evidence. The appworker account was created, /etc/security/limits.d/appworker.conf correctly sets nofile=8192 and nproc=256 (soft and hard), PAM pam_limits.so is active in the session stacks, and live ulimit verification as the appworker user confirmed both limits. The node-restart protocol is fully satisfied: pre-restart boot ID (19062a82…) was captured, shutdown issued, connection drop and polling observed, node returned online, and post-restart boot ID (8ad0f94b…) is distinct and corroborated by the lifecycle after_executor snapshot. Account and limits were confirmed intact post-reboot. Minor hygiene issue: the /tmp/appworker-limits.conf staging file was left behind after the reboot.
limitations: The sudo -u appworker ulimit probe tests limits inherited from the invoking sudo session rather than a full PAM login session; however, pam_limits.so is confirmed active in both system-auth and password-auth, making the effective value highly reliable.

The /tmp/appworker-limits.conf residue was observed in the after_executor snapshot but its content was not re-read post-reboot to confirm it survived (it is a /tmp file and may have been recreated or retained; either way it is harmless residue).

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands serve a clear task or protocol purpose: useradd created the required account, the limits.d write configured the required limits, and the reboot fulfilled the node-restart evidence protocol. One hygiene issue: /tmp/appworker-limits.conf (the staging file written in cmd-8b0a60bbdf6242ae before being copied to /etc/security/limits.d/appworker.conf) was not cleaned up and remains present in the after_executor temporary-files snapshot. This is low-risk residue but constitutes an unnecessary retention of a staging artifact. No unnecessary mutations were performed, no services were damaged, no security controls were weakened, and no conflicting configuration was introduced.
